(2) THE BOUND TEST PASSED LOCALLY AND FAILED ON CI, on the platform rather than on the bound. The megabyte child asserted against its own output and CI measured 183,296 bytes of the intended 5,120,000, so `originalBytes > 4e6` was false. Cause: `process.stdout.write` to a PIPE is ASYNCHRONOUS on POSIX, so a child that calls `process.exit` right after a large write loses whatever is still queued in userspace; on Windows (where the local run passed) a pipe write is synchronous, which is why the same child delivered all of it. Fixed by making every fake bake write through `fs.writeSync` on the raw fd (commit ae8a9e6), which cannot lose bytes on either platform. Recorded because the general form is worth carrying: a test whose subject is a bound must not be decidable by the runtime's write buffering.

missionPremise: A bake that refused left nothing behind that could answer WHY. The 2026-09-19 Williamson run's 11 Cloud Logging entries said nothing but BAKE_FAILED, and `run_events` held `termination {"reason":"BAKE_FAILED"}`; both strings were produced from `err.code` alone, while the child's own words existed in memory for the life of the process and nowhere else. The cause had to be inferred from a store read (P-351's per-keyspace blast-radius guard), and the second mechanism could not be closed.
completionPredicate: On a subprocess failure from a bake call site, a bounded tail (bytes and lines, stated) of stderr AND stdout is written to the run's durable record and to the job log before the job exits; a child that names its refusal keeps that name in `runs.refuse_code`, with BAKE_FAILED reserved for a failure with no name; every runShell caller is enumerated and either fixed or named; and the behaviour is shown by a fake bake that violates it in both directions.
scopeBasis: The dispatch's own scope: hauska-factory only, no store writes, no deploys, no merges; the subject is the bake subprocess failure path in the publish and dollar-fields jobs. Every other runShell/spawn caller is NAMED rather than absorbed, and nothing in LDT, engine, map or MCP is touched.
theFalsifiers: F1 (a named refusal keeps its name): a fake tier1-conformant bake printing `ACCOUNT_KEYED_BLAST_RADIUS: 48209 numeric=319480 r=143184` and exiting 1 -> `err.code === 'ACCOUNT_KEYED_BLAST_RADIUS'`, `refuseNameSource === 'stderr'`, `step === 'node-facet-bake-tier1-conformant'`, `exitCode === 1`, both tails carry the child's lines. BEFORE, on the SAME child error: the removed wrapper yields `code === 'BAKE_FAILED'` and `refusalRecordFor` returns null, so recordSubprocessRefusal writes ZERO rows. Both directions executed.

F2 (a failure with NO name still records BAKE_FAILED plus its tail): a child printing `kaboom: could not open the parcel store` -> `code === BAKE_FAILED`, `named === false`, and ONE run_events row whose stderr tail carries the line. The negative direction is the naming rule itself: `ERROR:`, `WARNING:`, `BP-LEDGER-01` and `HAUSKA_MCP_DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL required` all resolve to null -- no line is minted into a name it does not own.

F3 (the bound holds and cannot hide the name): ~5MB of stdout in 1KB lines then the refusal on the last stderr line -> `originalBytes > 4e6`, `bytes <= 8192`, both bound flags true, the name STILL read (it is taken from the raw stream; the tail is bounded after), and the formatted log line under 20KB. Unit cases both directions: 100 lines -> last 40; a 5MB single line -> last 8192 bytes; a multi-byte code point straddling the cut survives whole (3-byte `€`, no U+FFFD); empty and null inputs give the empty record instead of throwing.

F4 (the name reaches the RUN ROW, not only the record): through the whole runBastropPublish with a real bake subprocess -> `runs.refuse_code === 'ACCOUNT_KEYED_BLAST_RADIUS'`, one run_events row of kind subprocess-refusal naming the step, the exit status and both tails; the TERMINATION event's reason is the child's name (`assert.notEqual(..., BAKE_FAILED)`), where the incident recorded BAKE_FAILED; and `publish_runs.length === 0`, so a refused bake records no success.

F5 (the cli.mjs edge is safe for the ~50 jobs that share that catch): a tailed subprocess failure prints code + step/exit/childName + both bounded tails; an error with no tails (`STAGING_TARGET_MISSING`, or a plain `new Error('boom')`) prints exactly `err.code || err.message`, character for character what the line printed before; null prints 'unknown failure'.

F6 (a spawn failure is not a refusal, and vice versa): `{code: 'ENOENT'}` (a string, so the child never ran) keeps ENOENT and reports `exitCode: null`; `{code: 1, stderr: 'ERROR: x'}` (a number, no name in the words) yields BAKE_FAILED with `exitCode: 1`. The resolution order is asserted rather than implied.

F7 (the dollar-fields wrapper, same shape, same fix): a real fake `dollar-fields.mjs` refusing -> `code` is the child's name and `step === 'dollar-fields'`; the removed wrapper on the same child error gives BAKE_FAILED and nothing recordable.

recordShape.insert: INSERT INTO run_events (run_id, kind, body) VALUES ($1,$2,$3::jsonb) -- the statement shape five other writers in this repo already use: no migration, no new column.

body.step: the bake stage that refused (node-facet-bake-tier1-conformant / node-facet-bake-tier2-conformant / parcels-pmtiles-bake / dollar-fields), so a record names WHICH child refused rather than 'a subprocess'
body.command: the first 8 argv words, so a reader can re-run the child by hand
body.refuseCode: the run's own refuse_code value: the child's name when it has one, else BAKE_FAILED, else a spawn errno
body.childRefuseName: the child's own printed name, or null, with `named` saying which of the two this is
body.exitCode: the numeric exit status, or null when the child never ran
body.bound: {bytes, lines} applied, travelling WITH the text so a reader never guesses whether they are looking at all of it
body.stderr: {text, bytes, lines, originalBytes, originalLines, truncated, truncatedBy}
body.stdout: the same shape -- stdout is not decoration: P-351's per-keyspace measurement is printed THERE

recordShape.bound: 8192 BYTES and 40 LINES, applied to each stream separately, line bound first then byte bound, the END of the stream kept, trimmed at a UTF-8 code-point boundary. Bytes are load-bearing because ONE line can be megabytes. Every record carries the pre-bound size and which bound fired.
recordShape.writtenWhereAndWhen: in runBastropPublish's catch, AFTER `UPDATE runs SET status='failed', refuse_code=...` (so the NAME is durable even if the event write fails) and BEFORE terminateOrRecordConflict (so the termination record the incident measured is still written). A failed record write is reported on stderr LOUDLY and never thrown: throwing would replace the refusal with the record-write error and lose the termination record too.
recordShape.whyNotJustTheMessage: Keeping the words in the Error's message (what the removed code did) is not a record: the message dies with the process, and the deployed edge printed only the code.

threeQuestionGate.whatWritesTheReason: `recordSubprocessRefusal` in src/lib/subprocess-refusal.mjs, called from runBastropPublish's catch (bastrop-publish.mjs) and runDollarFieldsPatch's catch (dollar-fields-patch.mjs): one run_events row of kind `subprocess-refusal`, plus the run row's `refuse_code` carrying the child's name. The job LOG is written by the same module's `formatSubprocessFailureForLog`, printed by the jobs' top-level catches and by src/cli.mjs's catch, which is the deployed edge.
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggersIt: ANY subprocess failure from those two bake call sites -- the conformant tier-1/tier-2 bake, the parcels-pmtiles bake and the dollar-fields bake -- on any target, in any environment, whether the child refused with a name, refused without one, or failed to spawn. There is no flag and nothing to remember.
threeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenTheReasonIsMissing: The refusal becomes UNANSWERABLE: the run row says BAKE_FAILED, the log says BAKE_FAILED, and the measurement that identifies the cause existed only inside a process that has exited -- which is what happened on 2026-09-19, where the cause had to be inferred from a store read and the second mechanism could not be closed. BAKE_FAILED is indistinguishable from every other nameless bake failure.
whatBypassesIt: A HARD KILL that skips the handler (SIGKILL, OOM, the platform's task kill). The catch never runs, so no `subprocess-refusal` row exists. How the record reads then, named precisely: the run row is still in-flight, the reaper later terminates it with the EXECUTION's exit kind (crashed/killed/timeout, exit_kindFromExecution) and the reaper as recorder, and `refuse_code` stays whatever it was -- null. The child's output is LOST, not merely unrecorded: runShell PIPES the child's stdio, so the child's words never reach Cloud Logging either.

A SIGTERM / Cloud Run CANCEL is a different handler and a different record: control/runs.mjs's sigterm guard writes exit_kind 'killed', recorder sigterm-guard, reason 'external SIGTERM'. Also no subprocess-refusal row and no captured tail.

A BAKE INVOKED OUTSIDE THESE TWO CALL SITES: a hand-run of the bundled CLI (`node /app/bakes/tier1-conformant.mjs ...`) prints its own refusal to its own stderr and leaves nothing in the factory store; the child's own `console.error(err.code || err.message)` is the only record, and it is whatever the operator kept.

The exit STATUS a bake refusal reports is unchanged (1): the child's names are not in src/lib/scope-refusal-exits.mjs's declaration table (COUNTY_NO_SOURCE_PENDING, COUNTY_NOT_IN_SCOPE), so nothing a bake prints can be read as a parent-continuable declaration. Named as a boundary rather than left implicit, because the name now flows into exitCodeForRefusal.

leave_behind: src/lib/subprocess-refusal.mjs is importable by ANY job in this repo and is not bake-specific: a job that spawns anything and wants the child's words on the record imports `subprocessFailure` + `recordSubprocessRefusal` + `formatSubprocessFailureForLog` and passes a `step`. The bound and the naming rule are the module's, not the caller's, so two jobs cannot disagree about what a name is.

THE DEPLOYED EDGE FOR EVERY FACTORY JOB IS src/cli.mjs, NOT THE JOB FILE. Dockerfile.publish's ENTRYPOINT is `node src/cli.mjs` and cloudbuild.publish.yaml passes the subcommand as an arg, so a job file's own `if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith('<job>.mjs'))` block never runs on Cloud Run. Any future change to 'what the log says when a job fails' must land in cli.mjs or it lands nowhere -- read the entrypoint, never the file the dispatch points at. This is the single most transferable fact this lane produced.

The bake CLIs report a refusal ONLY through their words: they end `main().catch((err) => { console.error(err.code || err.message); process.exit(1); })`, so there is no exit payload, no last-line JSON and no exit-code map -- every refusal exits 1. A name can therefore be read ONLY from the child's last non-empty line, and the tail is the only carrier of the measurement. If a future bake is given a structured refusal contract, the naming rule's `namedRefusalFromOutput` is the one place to change.

The naming rule is deliberately conservative: SCREAMING_SNAKE (at least one underscore), alone on the line or followed by a colon, <= 96 chars. Single words like ERROR/WARNING are NOT names, because a wrong name in `refuse_code` is worse than none -- refused precision, never the words.

Write fakes with fs.writeSync, not process.stdout.write. On POSIX a pipe write is asynchronous and a child that exits immediately loses queued bytes (measured: 183,296 of 5,120,000 on CI). Any test that measures a bound over a real child must not be decidable by the platform's write buffering.

`runs.status` on a refused publish is written TWICE and the second writer wins: the job's catch sets 'failed', then control/termination.mjs sets the TERMINATION record's own exit_kind, which is 'failure' for a non-dry-run refusal. Assertions about that column must name which writer they mean; `refuse_code` is the refusal's own field and is not overwritten.

The next surface for this row's question is src/jobs/publish-gate-sched.mjs (the gate rail: its refusals' words still live only in the process, while its code is stable and its stdout/stderr fields are already read by P-195/P-201), then src/control/cloudrun-jobs.mjs (JOB_EXECUTE_FAILED with gcloud's words in the message).

The bound protects the RECORD and the LOG LINE; it does not bound what execFile buffers (the call sites allow 20MB). A child that prints more fails with ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER, which the module keeps as the errno (failing to RUN is a different fact from refusing) and records with whatever partial output the error carries.
fleetMemory: Three things other lanes should take rather than rediscover: (1) the deployed entrypoint is the edge -- read Dockerfile/cloudbuild, not the job file; (2) a new shared module under src/lib is the cheap way to make one behaviour true for every caller, and the tests for it can be real-child tests with no store at all; (3) a test that passes on Windows and fails on Linux is usually a runtime-semantics difference (here: async pipe writes), so when CI contradicts a local pass, the platform is a hypothesis to test before the code is.
whatRemainsOpen: THE LIVE OBSERVATION: the first real bake refusal after the seat merges and deploys. Until a real run refuses, the claim that a future refusal is answerable in Cloud Logging and in run_events is a claim about a code path, not about a record. This lane does not claim otherwise.
publish-gate-sched.mjs's gate-CLI refusals still leave their words only in the process (named above, not fixed).
cloudrun-jobs.mjs's gcloud failures still become JOB_EXECUTE_FAILED with the words in the message (named above, not fixed).
A HARD KILL still loses the child's output entirely, and the record then reads as the reaper's exit kind. That is a property of the handler being skipped rather than a defect this row can close.
